locate_in_source: Located in shra-2025-10-28 (20 pages, born-digital text). Part I, SHRA Property Eligibility Criteria, page 2, states the lot-size limits and the qualified-urban-uses test. question_for_human_reviewer: The memo (page 2) states that multifamily-zoned lots must be less than 5 acres and single-family-zoned lots under 1.5 acres and vacant, and FAQ Q.1 (page 12) lists the single-family zones. Do you agree that each limit is a strict less-than on the pre-subdivision lot area, that the single-family zone list is exhaustive, and that this criterion should be split into a zone-category criterion and one lot-area criterion per path? Which official source defines multifamily-zoned lots, given that the memo does not list those zones?

candidate_components.label: Lot area limit for a multifamily-zoned lot: less than 5 acres
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, SHRA Property Eligibility Criteria, page 2 (lot-size paragraph)

excerpts.text: To qualify, multifamily-zoned lots must be less than 5 acres, and single-family zoned lots must be under 1.5 acres and "vacant." (See FAQ Section, Q.1.)

new_facts_needed: shra-zone-category, recorded by a human (see la_shra.zone-category).
candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: lot-area stays a number in sq ft and must be the area of the lot to be subdivided, from a reviewed record. 5 acres = 217,800 sq ft.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: If shra-zone-category is multifamily: lot-area < 217,800 sq ft -> consistent_with_source; lot-area >= 217,800 sq ft -> disqualifying_per_source. Missing or conflicting lot area -> unknown or conflict. Any other zone category: this component does not apply.
judgment_or_ambiguity: 'Less than 5 acres' is read as strictly less than; confirm against GCS 66499.41.
The memo does not say whether a designated remainder parcel (AB 130, FAQ Q.23) counts toward the lot area.
The acre-to-square-foot conversion is not stated in the memo.

candidate_components.label: Lot area limit for a single-family-zoned lot: under 1.5 acres (vacancy stays separate)
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo Part I, SHRA Property Eligibility Criteria, page 2 (lot-size paragraph)

excerpts.text: To qualify, multifamily-zoned lots must be less than 5 acres, and single-family zoned lots must be under 1.5 acres and "vacant." (See FAQ Section, Q.1.)

new_facts_needed: shra-zone-category, recorded by a human (see la_shra.zone-category).
candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: lot-area in sq ft of the lot to be subdivided. 1.5 acres = 65,340 sq ft.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: If shra-zone-category is single_family_listed: lot-area < 65,340 sq ft -> consistent_with_source for the area limit only; lot-area >= 65,340 sq ft -> disqualifying_per_source. The same sentence requires the lot to be vacant; that stays requires_judgment under la_shra.vacant-site-definition.
judgment_or_ambiguity: 'Under 1.5 acres' is read as strictly less than.
Vacancy is a legal definition (FAQ Q.1, page 12). A consistent area result says nothing about vacancy and must never be inferred from structure counts.

candidate_components.label: SHRA zone category: the memo's single-family zone list versus multifamily-zoned
candidate_components.pinpoint: Memo FAQ Q.1, page 12 (definition of zoned for single-family residential development)

excerpts.text: Zoned for single-family residential development means sites in the following zones: A1, A2, RA, RE, RS, R1, RU, RZ, and RW1.

new_facts_needed: shra-zone-category: controlled, human-recorded; never parsed from the free-text zoning string.
candidate_components.controlled_value_encoding: single_family_listed: base zone is A1, A2, RA, RE, RS, R1, RU, RZ, or RW1. multifamily: a human records that the base zone permits multifamily residential development. neither: it permits neither. undetermined: otherwise.
candidate_components.proposed_rule_if_reviewer_agrees: single_family_listed -> the single-family path (1.5-acre limit plus the vacancy judgment). multifamily -> the multifamily path (5-acre limit). neither -> disqualifying_per_source only if the reviewer confirms the two categories are exhaustive. undetermined -> requires_judgment.
judgment_or_ambiguity: The single-family list is a definition ('means'), so it reads as exhaustive. The memo gives no list for multifamily-zoned lots.
Whether R2, RD, and commercial zones that permit housing count as multifamily-zoned is not stated.
Zone variations and suffixes (R1 variation zones, Q conditions, D limitations) need a human classification.
The memo pertains to Chapter 1 of the Zoning Code only (page 1); a Chapter 1A parcel stays with la_shra.implementation-memo-scope.
